issue: Is the Sentencing Guidelines commentary to § 4B1.2 (Application Note 1), which treats attempt, conspiracy, and aiding-and-abetting as 'controlled substance offenses,' consistent with the guideline text, which does not list inchoate offenses?

sides.position: The commentary is consistent with the guideline text and may properly include inchoate offenses in the definition of controlled substance offense.
cases: United States v. Lewis, 963 F.3d 16 (1st Cir. 2020)
United States v. Richardson, 958 F.3d 151 (2d Cir. 2020)
United States v. Smith, 989 F.3d 575 (7th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Vea-Gonzales, 999 F.2d 1326 (9th Cir. 1993)
United States v. Smith, 54 F.3d 690 (11th Cir. 1995)

sides.position: The commentary is inconsistent with § 4B1.2(b) because the guideline does not enumerate inchoate offenses, so the commentary cannot expand the definition.
cases: United States v. Nasir, 982 F.3d 144 (3d Cir. 2020) (en banc)
United States v. Campbell, 22 F.4th 438 (4th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Havis, 927 F.3d 382 (6th Cir. 2019) (en banc)
United States v. Winstead, 890 F.3d 1082 (D.C. Cir. 2018)

quote: The circuit courts are divided on the legitimacy of this application note, with a slight majority finding the guideline text and application note consistent with one another.
cite: United States v. Babcock, 40 F.4th 1172 (10th Cir. 2022)
